pr_title: Fix decoders so that they use the passed in propq.
pr_body:
Fixes #21198

Inside the decoder fetches were passing propq as NULL. The problem stems from lower level OSSL_DECODER objects only handling the libctx and using NULL as the propq. (This happens because we can normally get the libctx from the provctx, and that is what is passed down). This PR add a newctx_ex() method to the OSSL_DECODER object which passes an extra arg for the propq. It will use this new method if it exists, otherwise it uses the old newctx().
I considered using the set_ctx_params method but it is cleaner when implemented as a new_ex constructor.

This does not attempt to address the encoders passing a propq.

pr_comments: Put it in draft form for feedback.. Tested locally.

This is very invasive in `crypto/encode_decode` and for providers...  just to pass a property query string?

I would have expected something like this (yes yes, with the param key as a macro rather than a direct string):

``` diff
diff --git a/crypto/encode_decode/decoder_pkey.c b/crypto/encode_decode/decoder_pkey.c
index 79b120b95c..7e0a0cb08e 100644
--- a/crypto/encode_decode/decoder_pkey.c
+++ b/crypto/encode_decode/decoder_pkey.c
@@ -378,6 +378,12 @@ int ossl_decoder_ctx_setup_for_pkey(OSSL_DECODER_CTX *ctx,
     struct decoder_pkey_data_st *process_data = NULL;
     struct collect_data_st collect_data = { NULL };
     STACK_OF(EVP_KEYMGMT) *keymgmts = NULL;
+    OSSL_PARAM decoder_params[] = {
+        OSSL_PARAM_END,
+        OSSL_PARAM_END
+    };
+
+    decoder_params[0] = OSSL_PARAM_construct_utf8_string("properties", propquery, 0);
 
     OSSL_TRACE_BEGIN(DECODER) {
         const char *input_type = ctx->start_input_type;
@@ -455,7 +461,8 @@ int ossl_decoder_ctx_setup_for_pkey(OSSL_DECODER_CTX *ctx,
      * be nonzero. Else nothing was found and we do nothing.
      */
     if (OSSL_DECODER_CTX_get_num_decoders(ctx) != 0) {
-        if (!OSSL_DECODER_CTX_set_construct(ctx, decoder_construct_pkey)
+        if (!OSSL_DECODER_CTX_set_params(ctx, decoder_params)
+            || !OSSL_DECODER_CTX_set_construct(ctx, decoder_construct_pkey)
             || !OSSL_DECODER_CTX_set_construct_data(ctx, process_data)
             || !OSSL_DECODER_CTX_set_cleanup(ctx,
                                              decoder_clean_pkey_construct_arg))
```

The rest should happen *entirely* in the decoders where this parameter is interesting.

We do have this pattern elsewhere...
e.g void *OSSL_FUNC_signature_newctx(void *provctx, const char *propq);
And I would still have to add a set_ctx_params to most ctx's since not many have that method..

I will try out your way and see what it looks like..

> And I would still have to add a set_ctx_params to most ctx's since not many have that method..

This is untrue, a set_ctx_param function isn't mandatory.  If it isn't in a particular OSSL_DISPATCH, a call won't be attempted:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/2525109f90cf3a91a909621266ec6854a83805e2/crypto/encode_decode/decoder_meth.c#L657-L660
(setters and getters should generally *never* be mandatory)

@levitte any ideas what to do with OSSL_DECODER_CTX_add_extra()?
It can add  epki2pki, spkitypespki, pem2der.. after the ossl_decoder_ctx_setup_for_pkey.
epki2pki needs to do the set_ctx_params call...

Looks like I can delay the set_ctx params until after the OSSL_DECODER_CTX_add_extra()..

issue_context.title: PEM_read_bio_PrivateKey_ex() ignores the supplied property query
comments:
This is a bug..
Most encoders/decoders do not currently use propq inside their decode functions...

e.g. epki2pki_decode() calls PKCS12_pbe_crypt_ex(...., PROV_LIBCTX_OF(ctx->provctx), NULL);
where the NULL represents the propq.

Structures such as epki2pki_ctx_st do not contain a propq.

Also the newctx dispatch method does not pass it, and most ctx's dont have a set_ctx_params currently..

The only one that does handle a propq is key2any_set_ctx_params() which handles a cipher and propq via OSSL_ENCODER_CTX_set_cipher().

SO we would need to either handle set_ctx_params for most ctx's or have a new_ctx_ex() that passes the propq.
The workaround is to apply the `fips=yes` as the default property query instead.

> The workaround is to apply the `fips=yes` as the default property query instead.

The problem comes when a different query is needed for a specific use case, e.g. accessing a non-FIPS decoder when the default is fips.

I haven't found a viable workaround yet. Creating an entirely separate LIB_CTX may work (I have not had success yet) but is expensive.

All decoders are FIPS :grin: They might need non-FIPS algorithms to load stuff.

+1 for setting the default property query and disabling it while loading or setting it to `fips=?yes` (which isn't so safe).

An alternate libctx ought to be workable, although it's going to be messy if you want to move the key between libctxs.
An alternate libctx with a default property query of `fips=?yes` ought to be workable however.

Swapping the global property to something else and then swapping it back doesnt seem very safe.

Just to reiterate the decoder and encoder dispatch functions sitting inside the ctx objects, are currently passing NULL as the propq internally.
That the property query isn't applied is clearly a bug. Although I assume the fix will be quite invasive.

review_comments:
Note I have not tried to address this NULL here.. It may need a OSSL_DECODER_CTX_add_decoder_ex() that passes a propq.
I did not want to do that here for backport reasons.
I cant see anywhere where we use this function..
